hook: Four astronauts, coming home from the Moon. This was their window.
narration: Four astronauts were coming home from the Moon, and this was the view out their window.
This was Artemis II, hitting Earth's atmosphere on April 10, 2026.
A heat shield on the bottom of the capsule takes the heat of re-entry, so the cabin stays cool.
At their farthest, they had been two hundred fifty two thousand miles from home.
Then two small drogue parachutes opened to slow and steady the capsule.
[short pause] Next, three huge main parachutes bloomed outside the window.
outcome: Orion splashed down in the Pacific near San Diego, with all four astronauts aboard.
title: Artemis II re-entry from the window
description:
On April 10, 2026, a camera at the pilot's forward window of NASA's Artemis II Orion spacecraft recorded re-entry and parachute deployment before splashdown in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego.

Footage: NASA JSC video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/GP011149

extra_sources.excerpt: NASA's Orion spacecraft carrying Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialist Christina Koch from NASA, along with Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen from the CSA (Canadian Space Agency), splashes down in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California, at 5:07 p.m. PDT, (8:07 p.m. EDT) on Friday, April 10, 2026.

NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen splashed down at 5:07 p.m. PDT Friday off the coast of San Diego, completing a nearly 10-day journey that took them 252,756 miles from home at their farthest distance from Earth.
